title: emergencyTransfer leaves totalStaked / userInfo / rewardBalance non-zero while sweeping all tokens, permanently bricking user exit paths
rootCause: `emergencyTransfer` moves `phUSD.balanceOf(this)` and `rewardToken.balanceOf(this)` to an arbitrary recipient and then `_pause()`s the contract, but does not zero or reconcile any of `totalStaked`, `userInfo[*].amount`, `userInfo[*].phUSDDebt`, `userInfo[*].stableDebt`, `rewardBalance`, `accPhUSDPerShare`, `accStablePerShare`, `rewardPerSecond`. The contract's bookkeeping continues to claim users hold positions that the contract can no longer back.
impact: After invocation, every user-facing path is permanently broken: (a) the contract is paused, so `stake`/`withdraw`/`claim` revert via `whenNotPaused`; (b) `pauseWithdraw` is open but reverts at `phUSD.safeTransfer(msg.sender, amount)` because the contract holds zero phUSD -- so stakers cannot recover principal even in the emergency path; (c) `unpause` only re-opens `withdraw`, which again fails at the final `phUSD.safeTransfer`. The owner can refill off-chain, but on-chain there is no recovery path for users without owner action. Combined with the fact that `emergencyTransfer` has no `nonReentrant`, no `whenNotPaused`, and no recipient validation other than the value being uncoerced, this concentrates principal-loss risk on a single owner key.
attackVector: Single owner transaction. With one `onlyOwner` call, all staked principal and undistributed rewards leave the contract; users are left with internal ledger entries that cannot be redeemed on-chain. If the owner key is compromised, this is a single-tx rug. If the owner is honest, an off-chain process must redistribute funds back to users -- there is no on-chain claim mechanism after emergency.
steps: Multiple users stake phUSD; totalStaked = S > 0
owner.emergencyTransfer(attackerAddress) -- contract sends all phUSD and rewardToken to attackerAddress, then _pause()
user.pauseWithdraw(any amount) -- reverts inside SafeERC20.safeTransfer because phUSD balance is 0
owner.unpause -> user.withdraw(any amount) -- also reverts at safeTransfer
Internal state still says user.amount > 0 and totalStaked = S, but no tokens back it
remediation: Either (a) reframe the function as a true 'abandon ship' by also zeroing `totalStaked`, `rewardBalance`, `accX`, and emitting a per-snapshot event the off-chain redistribution can use; (b) restrict the function to only sweeping the excess (`balanceOf - totalStaked` on the phUSD side, `balanceOf - rewardBalance` on the reward side), preserving the user-exit invariant; (c) add an on-chain post-emergency claim path that pays users pro-rata from a refill. At minimum require the recipient to be a non-zero, distinct address and emit a clearly-labeled event so off-chain bookkeeping can reconcile.
notes: Owner power is documented (centralization risk), but the on-chain DoS of pauseWithdraw is an independent implementation-level defect, not a pure centralization concern -- a benign owner who runs emergencyTransfer (e.g. to migrate to V2) still cannot let users escape via the documented emergency path.
